concepts.def: Kinetic, gravitational, elastic, thermal, chemical, etc.
Energy moved between stores mechanically, electrically, by heating or radiation.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Energy is what makes things happen. Without it, nothing moves, nothing heats, nothing lights up.

Energy is measured in joules (J). A small chocolate bar holds about 1,000,000 J!

Energy can be stored in different ways - we call these energy stores.

Scientists list 8 stores of energy:

Chemical (food/fuel), Kinetic (movement), Gravitational (height), Elastic (stretched/squashed), Thermal (heat), Magnetic (magnets), Electrostatic (charge), Nuclear (atoms).

Each is just energy waiting to be used.

A petrol-filled car has chemical store.

A book on a high shelf has gravitational store.

A speeding ball has kinetic store.

A stretched rubber band has elastic store.

Practice identifying which store each object has!

mcqs.q: A book on a high shelf has lots of energy in its:
options: kinetic store
gravitational store
chemical store
sound store

mcqs.q: Petrol stores energy in which form?
options: thermal
kinetic
chemical
gravitational

mcqs.q: Why is nuclear fusion much harder to achieve on Earth than fission?
options: Fusion requires extremely high temperatures and pressures to overcome the electrostatic repulsion between positive nuclei.
Fusion is harder because the materials are rarer than uranium.
Atoms emit only one colour each, determined by their temperature.
Fusion is harder because you need to break atoms apart first.

mcqs.q: Why do atoms emit light only at specific wavelengths rather than a continuous spectrum?
options: Fusion is harder because you need to break atoms apart first.
Atoms emit only one colour each, determined by their temperature.
Atoms can emit any wavelength, but only certain ones are visible.
Electrons occupy discrete energy levels; transitions between levels emit photons of specific frequencies (E = hf).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Energy store”?
options: Where energy is held until transferred — like kinetic, gravitational, chemical, thermal.
Energy can't be made or destroyed, only transferred from store to store.
Energy in food, fuel and batteries; released by reactions.
Energy in an object held high up; bigger if mass or height is bigger.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Energy is conserved”?
options: Energy can't be made or destroyed, only transferred from store to store.
Where energy is held until transferred — like kinetic, gravitational, chemical, thermal.
Energy in an object held high up; bigger if mass or height is bigger.
Energy in a moving object; faster and heavier objects have more.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Kinetic store”?
options: Energy in a moving object; faster and heavier objects have more.
Energy can't be made or destroyed, only transferred from store to store.
Energy in food, fuel and batteries; released by reactions.
Where energy is held until transferred — like kinetic, gravitational, chemical, thermal.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Gravitational store”?
options: Energy in an object held high up; bigger if mass or height is bigger.
Where energy is held until transferred — like kinetic, gravitational, chemical, thermal.
Energy in hotter objects; transferred when in contact with cooler ones.
Energy in food, fuel and batteries; released by reactions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Thermal store”?
options: Where energy is held until transferred — like kinetic, gravitational, chemical, thermal.
Energy in an object held high up; bigger if mass or height is bigger.
Energy in hotter objects; transferred when in contact with cooler ones.
Energy in a moving object; faster and heavier objects have more.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Chemical store”?
options: Energy in an object held high up; bigger if mass or height is bigger.
Energy in food, fuel and batteries; released by reactions.
Energy in a moving object; faster and heavier objects have more.
Where energy is held until transferred — like kinetic, gravitational, chemical, thermal.
